learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the true depth of Yoga beyond physical fitness! Understand its philosophical roots, the eight limbs of Patanjali, and its path to inner peace.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Yoga comes from the Sanskrit root 'Yuj', meaning 'to join' or 'to unite'. It is not merely stretching; it is the philosophical practice of uniting the individual self (Atman) with the universal consciousness (Brahman) to achieve liberation.

Sage Patanjali compiled the foundational text of Yoga philosophy around 200 BCE. He defined Yoga as 'Chitta Vritti Nirodhah'—which means the stopping (nirodhah) of the fluctuations/chatter (vritti) of the mind (chitta).

The path to focus the mind has 8 steps. The first four are external preparations: 1. Yama (Social ethics like non-violence), 2. Niyama (Personal discipline like purity), 3. Asana (Physical postures for stability), 4. Pranayama (Breath control).

The next four are internal practices: 5. Pratyahara (Withdrawal of senses from distractions), 6. Dharana (Focused concentration on one point), 7. Dhyana (Continuous meditation), and 8. Samadhi (Ultimate state of spiritual absorption).

While modern society heavily focuses on Asanas for physical fitness and stress relief, the traditional Knowledge Practice of India views Yoga as a complete lifestyle guide for mental clarity, moral living, and spiritual enlightenment.

fun_activity.title: 🧠 The Trataka Focus Test
fun_activity.instructions: Light a candle or place a small dot on the wall at eye level. Sit comfortably and stare at it without blinking for as long as possible. This is an ancient concentration technique called 'Trataka', which builds the foundation for Dharana (Focus)!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize Patanjali's definition: 'Yogas Chitta Vritti Nirodhah' (Yoga is the cessation of the modifications of the mind).
📌 Be able to list the 8 limbs of Ashtanga Yoga in the correct sequence.
📌 Clearly distinguish between Yama (how you interact with the outside world/others) and Niyama (how you discipline your own self).
quick_recap: ⭐ Yoga is one of the six orthodox (Astika) schools of Indian philosophy.
⭐ Physical postures (Asanas) are only one small part (the 3rd limb) of the vast Yoga system.
⭐ The ultimate goal of Yoga is not flexibility, but 'Samadhi'—complete mental stillness and liberation.
